spots.name: Castillo San Felipe del Morro
spots.label: El Morro

text.directions_text: Head for Old San Juan and make for the Paseo del Morro. If you are already walking the waterfront, the free approach is from the Paseo de la Princesa end, following the sea wall towards the fort. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.
text.description:
El Morro is the great stone fortress at the north-western tip of Old San Juan, standing on a steep headland where the Atlantic meets the entrance to San Juan Bay. Building began in 1539 as a fortified tower, and by 1595 it had grown into a larger bastion fort. Work carried on for roughly two more centuries, and it reached its present form in 1787. The walls rise about 43 metres from the shoreline and are several metres thick, which is why the fort looks so solid in a photo. UNESCO listed it as a World Heritage Site in 1983.

It photographs well because the fort, the sea wall, the surf and the green slope can all sit in one frame. From here the fort is just to the east, close up and seen from the water side. Guides describe it as quieter than the main lawn, with clean backgrounds and good light towards sunset. The walkway can be reached on foot from the Paseo de la Princesa end. If you want a second view, the lawn in front of the fort shows the stone facade and lighthouse above the grass, with the horizon behind. Plaza del Quinto Centenario gives a higher angle back towards the castle from the city side.
text.geographic_location: In the Old San Juan historic quarter, on the north-western point of the old city's islet, where the headland guards the entrance to San Juan Bay. The Paseo del Morro walkway runs along the sea wall below the fort.
text.access_note: The Paseo del Morro walkway is reported to be free to walk from the Paseo de la Princesa end. One visitor review says entering the Paseo from the fort side carries a fee. The fort's interior and ramparts close in the late afternoon, so check the official site for current access before you go.

shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Sunset, according to several guides, when the walkway and lawn are the best places to be.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the fort's stone to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down a little so the sky keeps its colour. Take a few Live Photos or short bursts where the surf hits the wall, then pick the best frame. Wipe your lens first, as sea air can leave a film on it.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for a natural view of the fort. Switch to ultra-wide (0.5x) to fit the wall, surf and green slope into one frame. Use telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) for details such as the lighthouse or the stonework.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Paseo del Morro (the paved walkway that runs along the sea wall from the Raíces side up to the fort). The fort seen close up from the water side, with the wall, the surf and the lush slope in one frame. The fort is to the east of you. From here you see it close up from the water side, with the wall, the surf and the lush slope together.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and place the sea wall along a lower line so the fort rises above it. Keep the horizon level. For a different view, try the lawn in front of the fort, which shows the facade and lighthouse above the grass, or Plaza del Quinto Centenario for a higher angle looking back at the castle.

spots.alt: Castillo San Felipe del Morro, San Juan: the great stone fortress at the north-western tip of Old San Juan. Photo spot

spots.name: Isla Verde Beach
spots.label: Isla Verde Beach

text.directions_text: No Underground, tram or rail stops are listed for this spot, so start from Condado or Old San Juan and go east by taxi, or by AMA bus 5 or 53 to the Isla Verde bus terminal (about 1 hour from Old San Juan). Isla Verde is roughly 3 to 6 miles (4.8 to 9.7 km) east of those areas. Parking is reported to be difficult, so a taxi is the easier choice. The phone icon on the map is about 490 m south-east of the subject. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.
text.description: Isla Verde Beach is the long stretch of sand in front of one of the main tourist and resort areas of the San Juan metropolitan area. The name means "green island" in Spanish, after a small cay and reef a little way off the shore. The district is packed with hotels and condominiums, so you get a wide curve of golden sand and turquoise water with a skyline of buildings behind it. The beach also sits right next to Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport, so planes come in low over the water on their final approach. That means a passing aircraft can be your subject. Isla Verde is officially part of the municipality of Carolina, although it shares its coastline with Ocean Park and Condado, which are part of San Juan. For photos, stand on the sand near the waterline and decide first whether you want the planes or the beach and hotels. For the planes, wait for one to appear and keep plenty of sky above the sand. For the beach itself, keep the waves in the foreground and the hotel line on the far side. Parking nearby is reported to be difficult, so plan how you will arrive.
text.geographic_location: Isla Verde lies on the Atlantic coast east of Ocean Park and Condado, between the San Juan side of the metropolitan area and Piñones. It is technically in the municipality of Carolina, and the airport sits just to its south.
text.access_note: The beach is open shoreline, but access routes, parking and hotel areas may have their own rules, so check the official site before you go.

shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Afternoon is best for the planes over the beach. For the beach and hotel skyline lit by early sunlight, go in the early morning.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Take several shots as each plane passes, because the moment goes quickly. Check your first photo and adjust the exposure slider if the sky is washed out or the aircraft looks too dark.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Use the ultra-wide (0.5x) for the long beach and the hotel skyline, and the default lens (1x) for a planes-over-the-sand view. If your phone has telephoto/zoom (2x-5x), it brings an approaching aircraft closer, but keep some sky around it.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand about 490 m south-east of the subject, at the phone icon on the map, and face north-west. Stand on Playa Isla Verde, on the sand facing northeast toward the airport approach path, with the sea and the beach in front of you. From the shoreline you can frame low aircraft on final approach to Luis Muñoz Marín Airport against the sky above the beach.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and put the horizon on the lower line, leaving two thirds of the frame for sky, so a plane has room to cross it. Tap on the plane or the sky to focus, then drag the exposure slider down slightly so the aircraft stays crisp and the sky keeps its colour. For a different view, shoot along the sand with the ultra-wide (0.5x), keeping the turquoise water in the foreground and the hotels on the far side. Balneario del Escambrón is an alternative viewpoint from further along the coast, showing the Condado/Ocean Park and Isla Verde waterfront from a distance.

spots.alt: Isla Verde Beach, San Juan: the long stretch of sand in front of one. Photo spot

spots.name: Castillo San Cristóbal
spots.label: San Cristóbal Fort

text.directions_text: No station or tram stop is listed for this spot, so start from Old San Juan on foot. Once inside the fort, follow the ramparts on the Atlantic side to reach the sentry box. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.
text.description: Castillo San Cristóbal is the big stone fort on the Atlantic side of Old San Juan. For a phone photo, the best subject here is the Garita del Diablo, a small sentry box that juts out over the cliff at the sea's edge. It is the most photographed feature on the ocean side of the fort. It works well because it is a simple, strong shape with nothing behind it but the Atlantic, so there is little clutter to manage. The usual shot is taken from the rampart, looking back at the sentry box, with the sea filling the background. The grounds, ramparts and sentry box are part of a ticketed National Park Service site, so plan to go in rather than shoot from outside. Opening times can vary, so check the official site for current hours and tickets before you go. Start with the default lens (1x) so you can see the whole sentry box against the sea, then step back and try 2x for a tighter, flatter view. Tap the sentry box to focus, then slide the exposure down a little if the sky is washing out. Keep well back from the edge, and keep one hand firmly on the phone. If you want a second picture, the fort also gives a wide view over the rooftops of Old San Juan, the harbour and the Atlantic horizon. Plaza de Colón, which is free, shows the fort as a large stone mass at the end of the streets.
text.geographic_location: Castillo San Cristóbal is in Old San Juan, on the Atlantic-facing side of the old town. The Garita del Diablo shot is described separately: it is taken from the rampart, looking back at the sentry box.
text.access_note: The fort's grounds, ramparts and the Garita del Diablo are inside a ticketed National Park Service site, so check the official site before you go for current hours and entry.

shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Early morning, before the crowds arrive, gives the best chance of empty ramparts. Check the current opening time on the official site first.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the sentry box to lock focus, then drag the exposure slider down slightly so the sky keeps its colour and the stone keeps its detail. Take a few frames, because sea wind can make a handheld phone shake.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) to take in the whole sentry box and the sea behind it. Switch to 2x for a tighter shot that takes in less of the wall around it. Use the ultra-wide (0.5x) only if you want the whole rampart and sweep of coast in the frame.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject (outside the seaward wall, shot from the rampart looking back at the sentry box). The small sentry box jutting out over the cliff at the sea's edge, with the Atlantic filling the background. For the Garita del Diablo shot, stand on the rampart and look back at the sentry box, which sits out over the cliff, outside the seaward wall. The box should fill part of the frame, with the Atlantic filling the background behind it.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Switch on the gridlines and place the sentry box on one of the thirds, leaving the open sea and sky on the other side. Keep the horizon level. For a different view, the fort also gives a wide panorama over the Old San Juan rooftops and harbour, or you can shoot the fort from Plaza de Colón.
